profile.headline: Software Engineer II | Partner Manager (Ex-Google) | Social Entrepreneurship | Startup
profile.summary:
Dynamic backend engineer building in the crypto space. Previously wore multiple hats at Google—enabling ad partnerships, advising startups, and delivering technical solutions. Open to opportunities to apply technology for social impact and collaborate with thoughtful individuals and communities.

Tech stack: Golang, GraphQL, MongoDB

positions.title: Software Engineer II (Backend)
positions.description: • Build scalable backend for cryptocurrency use cases in real life

positions.title: Software Engineer (Backend)
positions.description:
• Develop and maintain product features that enable users to earn crypto rewards with ease (Golang, GraphQL, MongoDB)
• Led observability initiative to audit complex reward payment flow and implemented alerts and monitors that resulted in early incident detections
• Improved the platform's performance by completing a client call migration, resulting in a 60% reduction in P99 for the slowest endpoint.
• Facilitated integrating new cryptocurrencies to the platform by creating application UI for token project owners and admin tool for security, legal, and compliance teams to review and approve the listing process.

positions.title: Senior Partner Manager - Mobile Apps
positions.description:
• Build partnership with top mobile apps and gaming developers in North America.
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams solve business problems and consult strategic partners on monetization, user acquisition, and analytics for holistic growth.
• Lead the North America gaming initiatives to drive regional and global gaming growth.

positions.title: Advisor In Residence | Google for Startups
positions.description:
• Enabled mobile apps & gaming startups in Central Eastern Europe to grow.
• Acted as a dedicated advisor to 10 startups in the Google for Startups Accelerator program.

positions.title: Customer Relationship Assistant
positions.description:
• Helped design and set up the opening and closing procedures of a newly-opened location.
• Composed creative content for Facebook, the main online platform to converse with customers.
• Provided delightful customer experience and resolved difficult enquiries thanks to solid product knowledge, attention to details, and flexibility. 
• Made happy coffee, healthy food, and created smiles.

positions.title: Social Psychology Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Assisted Drs. Brittany Liu and Autumn Hostetter in a Social Psychology Research Project. 
• Designed survey questions using Qualtrics, run lab experiments with participants, and code behavioral research data.

positions.title: Library Desk Attendant
positions.description:
• 	Facilitated the circulation of library materials and the Michigan eLibrary service.
• 	Provided support on how to access and reserve materials to fellow students and the local community.

positions.title: Marketing and Operations Assistant
positions.description:
• Identified and successfully stewarded relationship with a wholesale buyer, and acted as liaison for business interactions. 
• Generated marketing materials in Photoshop to distribute on Facebook and via Mail Chimp. 
• Evaluated marketing ideas based on market research, Facebook Insights, and Google Analytics.
• Self-studied WordPress to upgrade and update the company’s website, which improved the site’s security and content.

positions.title: Value Chain Analysis Intern
positions.description:
• Designed an independent research project to analyze the value chains of cocoa beans in Vietnam with a focus on economic value added and UTZ environmental certification.
• Aggregated data through interviews with over 25 farmers, chocolate companies and local project officers in two provinces in the Eco-cocoa project. Completed a 112-page Honors thesis.

positions.title: Member of Class of 2013
positions.description:
• Got selected as the top 6.7% of over 600 applicants from all over the world to participate in an intensive summer career program that targets both professional development and community involvement.
• Participated in professional and technical training sessions as well as networking events that covered topics such as Finance, Excel, Consulting frameworks and Leadership.

positions.title: Barista
positions.description:
• 	Prepared and served drinks to a high volume of customers in a timely manner.
• 	Pleasantly greeted customers, personalized their orders, and performed cash registration accurately.

positions.title: Sales and Export Intern
positions.locationName: Marchena OE2-38 y Versalles, Santa Clara, Quito, Ecuador
positions.description:
• Received products from local producers and helped process transactions at the point of purchase.
• Assisted in marketing new products and publishing fair-trade events online. Started and managed the company's Facebook page to interact with consumers via social media.
• Researched potential markets in Europe for Ecuadorian handicraft and nutritive grains.

positions.title: International Studies Intern
positions.description:
•	Researched local resources and met deadlines for 5 proposals for the International Visitor Leadership Program to promote professional exchange across cultures in Kalamazoo, MI.
•	Communicated with national agencies to host international delegations and programs.
•       Accompanied and scheduled meetings for the Ukrainian Delegation during their 3-day visit to Kalamazoo to learn about youths in education and politics.

positions.title: Student Chaplain Intern
positions.description:
• 	Coordinated Community Reflection and Interfaith Council activities to promote mutual dialogues among students of various religious backgrounds.
• 	Collaborated with other student organizations to co-sponsor off-campus trips that introduce students to different religions and their practices.

honors.title: Member of Phi Beta Kappa Honor Society
honors.issuer: Issued by Phi Beta Kappa · Jun 2014

honors.title: The Beeler Fellowship
honors.description: Awarded for student projects conducted in international locations. Students must have proficiency in the foreign language and the ability to operate independently in an international environment.

projects.title: Senior Individualized Project
projects.description: Independent research project on the value chains of the cocoa bean industry in Vietnam with a focus on Ben Tre and Tien Giang provinces. Project awarded Honors in May 2014.

organizations.name: EnActUs
organizations.description:
•	Started and coordinated a group of 5 to collaborate with the College’s bookstore to promote fair-trade products and support better working conditions for people in disadvantaged communities. The total order value has reached over $3032.
•	Partner with the Ministry with Community to enable disadvantaged people to express creativity through designing and selling greeting cards.

organizations.name: Viet Youth Entrepreneurs Boot Camp (in collaboration with Stanford University)
organizations.description: • Led a group of 5 Vietnamese and Filipinos to win the third place in a business plan competition, as part of a one-week start-up course taught by Stanford Professor Thomas Kosnik
